usage: Used to describe someone who is comfortable and confident using modern electronic devices and software.
example_sentences: Our younger generation is incredibly tech-savvy.
You don't have to be tech-savvy to use this new software.
Being tech-savvy is almost a requirement for modern office jobs.
She's not very tech-savvy, so she struggled with the settings.
The company is looking for a tech-savvy assistant to manage their social media.
native_notes: Very common in both casual conversation and professional job descriptions.

usage: Used when referring to software, websites, or devices that are easy to understand and operate.
example_sentences: The new interface is much more user-friendly than the previous one.
We designed this app to be completely user-friendly for beginners.
Is the software user-friendly enough for elderly people?
The manual makes the whole setup process very user-friendly.
It's a user-friendly platform that doesn't require any technical training.
native_notes: You can use this to describe almost anything, not just software—like a coffee machine or a car dashboard.

uzbek: eng zamonaviy, eng yangi texnologiyalar bilan jihozlangan
usage: Used to describe something that uses the most modern and advanced technology available.
example_sentences: The hospital is equipped with state-of-the-art medical machinery.
Our office building features a state-of-the-art security system.
The company invested millions in state-of-the-art research facilities.
This car has a state-of-the-art navigation and sound system.
They use state-of-the-art software to track their global inventory.
native_notes: Often hyphenated when placed before the noun (e.g., 'a state-of-the-art computer').

uzbek: biror narsaga qattiq berilib qolmoq, bog'lanib qolmoq
usage: Used to describe an intense interest or addiction to a game, app, or social media platform.
example_sentences: I'm totally hooked on this new puzzle app.
Teenagers often get hooked on social media platforms for hours.
She got hooked on that online game during the lockdown.
He's hooked on watching tech reviews on YouTube.
I was hooked on the show after just the first episode.
native_notes: Very common in casual speech, specifically regarding 'screen time' and digital habits.

usage: Used in academic or social commentary to describe the gap between those who have access to technology and those who do not.
example_sentences: The government is trying to bridge the digital divide in rural areas.
The digital divide is becoming a major obstacle for online education.
COVID-19 highlighted the severity of the digital divide globally.
We need better infrastructure to overcome the digital divide.
Improving internet access is essential to narrowing the digital divide.
native_notes: A perfect phrase for IELTS Writing Task 2 or university essays about society and modern issues.

usage: Used to describe the most advanced stage in the development of technology.
common_mistakes: this is a cutting-edge (needs a noun after)
example_sentences: The company is famous for its cutting-edge research in AI.
We are using cutting-edge software to analyze the data.
This device represents the cutting-edge of mobile innovation.
The clinic offers cutting-edge medical treatments.
I am looking for a laptop with cutting-edge features.
native_notes: Used often in business and academic contexts to emphasize superiority.

usage: Refers to the information about a person that exists online as a result of their online activity.
example_sentences: Everything you post contributes to your digital footprint.
Employers often check your digital footprint before hiring you.
It is hard to erase your digital footprint once you've posted something.
Young people should be aware of the long-term impact of their digital footprint.
Managing your digital footprint is vital for privacy.
native_notes: Highly relevant for IELTS Writing Task 2 essays regarding social media, privacy, or security.

uzbek: ko'zi ekranga qadalib qolmoq, ekran oldidan ketolmay qolmoq
usage: A vivid idiomatic expression describing someone staring intensely at a computer, phone, or TV for a long time.
grammar_pattern: Subject + be + glued to the screen
common_mistakes: 'My eyes are glued to the screen' (usually used as the whole person)
example_sentences: I spent the whole night glued to the screen watching the election results.
It's unhealthy to be glued to the screen for hours on end.
The children are completely glued to the screen playing video games.
Stop being glued to the screen and come eat dinner with us!
Many office workers are glued to the screen from nine to five.
collocations: be glued to the screen for hours
native_notes: Use this in Speaking Part 1 or 3 when discussing the disadvantages of technology or modern lifestyle.

expression: keep up with the latest trends
uzbek: eng yangi tendensiyalardan xabardor bo'lib turmoq
usage: Used when talking about staying updated with fast-moving technological developments.
common_mistakes: follow up with the trends (Confusing with 'follow up')
alternatives: stay on top of current trends
example_sentences: It is difficult to keep up with the latest trends in mobile phone technology.
Companies must innovate to keep up with the latest trends in the industry.
I try to keep up with the latest trends, but technology changes too fast.
She uses social media to keep up with the latest trends in fashion.
The software updates automatically to help users keep up with the latest trends.
native_notes: Often used with a sense of slight difficulty or effort, given how quickly technology shifts.

usage: Used to describe someone who is confident and skilled at using modern technology.
common_mistakes: saying 'tech-savvy person' too often instead of just the adjective
example_sentences: The younger generation is generally much more tech-savvy than their grandparents.
You don't need to be overly tech-savvy to figure out how this new app works.
Our company is looking for tech-savvy candidates who can handle complex software.
Being tech-savvy has become a essential skill for almost any modern job.
She is incredibly tech-savvy and manages all our social media accounts.
native_notes: Very common in both professional interviews and casual conversation. It implies a practical skill set rather than just theoretical knowledge.

usage: Used when referring to a new product, technology, or event that significantly changes the way things are done.
grammar_pattern: Subject + be + a game-changer for + noun
common_mistakes: saying 'a big change' instead of the idiomatic 'game-changer'
using it for small, insignificant updates
example_sentences: The introduction of high-speed internet was a total game-changer for remote workers.
Many analysts believe that AI will be a massive game-changer for the healthcare industry.
This new software feature is a real game-changer for my daily productivity.
Virtual reality is expected to be a game-changer in the world of online education.
His discovery proved to be a game-changer for our research team.
native_notes: Used widely in business and journalism to describe innovation. It carries a positive, transformative tone.

usage: Used to describe software, hardware, or websites that are easy to use and intuitive.
common_mistakes: using 'user-friendly' for people instead of things
example_sentences: The interface is very user-friendly, even for those who are not tech-savvy.
We need to make our website more user-friendly to attract more customers.
Most people prefer apps that are simple and user-friendly.
The new operating system is not exactly user-friendly for older people.
Designers must focus on creating a user-friendly experience.
native_notes: This is standard terminology in tech product development. If a device is annoying to use, native speakers often say it is 'not very intuitive' rather than 'not user-friendly'.

uzbek: doimo aloqada bo'lmoq (internet yoki texnologiya orqali)
usage: Refers to maintaining communication or access to information via technology.
example_sentences: Smartphones make it so easy to stay connected with family abroad.
I need a reliable Wi-Fi connection to stay connected during my business trip.
It is becoming increasingly difficult to stay connected while travelling in remote areas.
Social media allows us to stay connected with friends from school.
We need to find better ways to stay connected in the digital age.
native_notes: This is a versatile phrase. It can refer to digital connectivity (internet) or interpersonal relationships sustained through tech.

usage: Used when a new product or technology completely changes the way things are done in a particular field.
common_mistakes: using it as an adjective (e.g., 'this is game-changer')
example_sentences: The invention of the smartphone was a real game-changer for communication.
AI is proving to be a game-changer in the healthcare industry.
This software was a game-changer for small business owners.
Electric vehicles could be a game-changer for the environment.
Remote work has been a game-changer for many employees.
native_notes: Very popular in business and tech news; implies a positive shift.

expression: to keep up with the times
usage: To stay updated with modern trends and changes in technology.
grammar_pattern: Subject + keep up with + the times
example_sentences: You have to upgrade your skills if you want to keep up with the times.
Many traditional companies are struggling to keep up with the times.
He reads tech blogs every day to keep up with the times.
It is difficult to keep up with the times when technology changes so quickly.
Our education system needs to change to keep up with the times.
collocations: struggle to keep up with the times
need to keep up with the times
keep up with the changing times
effort to keep up with the times
failing to keep up with the times
native_notes: Often used to explain why people or companies must adopt new technology to survive.

uzbek: tub burilish yasamoq, vaziyatni tubdan o'zgartirmoq
usage: Used when a new piece of technology or an idea significantly alters the way something is done.
common_mistakes: it is a game of change
it is game changing the situation
example_sentences: The introduction of high-speed internet was a total game changer for remote work.
This new AI software is a real game changer in the medical field.
Mobile banking has been a game changer for people living in rural areas.
If they launch that feature, it will be a game changer for the industry.
Remote sensing technology was a game changer for climate researchers.
collocations: proven to be a game changer
native_notes: Can be used as a noun phrase 'a game changer' or as an adjective 'a game-changing event'.

expression: to keep up with the latest trends
uzbek: eng so'nggi trendlardan xabardor bo'lib turmoq
usage: Used to describe the effort to remain updated with rapidly changing technology.
common_mistakes: following the last trends (using 'last' instead of 'latest')
alternatives: to stay on top of the latest developments
example_sentences: It is exhausting trying to keep up with the latest trends in smartphone technology.
Companies need to keep up with the latest trends to remain competitive.
I use social media to keep up with the latest tech trends.
He struggles to keep up with the latest trends in computer hardware.
It is impossible to keep up with the latest trends when tech changes daily.
native_notes: Use 'latest' for things that are new or most recent; do not confuse it with 'last' which means final.

usage: Used when technology is no longer effective, useful, or modern due to newer advancements.
example_sentences: Using paper records is becoming increasingly outdated in hospitals.
The software we are using is completely outdated and slow.
Most of the computers in the lab are now considered outdated.
He refuses to switch to a smartphone because he thinks they are outdated.
The equipment is outdated and needs to be replaced immediately.
native_notes: Obsolete is a stronger word, often implying that something is no longer produced or used at all.

usage: Used when software, an app, or a system has small technical errors or isn't working smoothly.
common_mistakes: using 'glitchy' as a noun instead of an adjective
confusing it with 'buggy' (they are similar but 'glitchy' often refers to performance stutter)
example_sentences: The game was so glitchy that I had to restart my console three times.
Is it just me, or is the new website version a bit glitchy today?
Don't download the update yet; I heard it’s really glitchy.
Video calls often get glitchy when the Wi-Fi signal is weak.
I find the streaming service quite glitchy on my mobile device.
native_notes: Very common in everyday speech when complaining about devices or apps.
